patients.summary: Healthy graduate student who joined the practice in 2021. Sexual assault in summer 2022 with an ED visit, post-exposure prophylaxis and an acute stress reaction that settled with counseling; routine preventive care since. Primary genital HSV diagnosed at an outside ED in July 2026, after her last practice visit.

documents.title: New Patient Inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is starting a graduate program this month and just moved to Florence. Wants a primary doctor locally rather than only the campus clinic. Has the university student health plan; card info entered. No current health issues per caller. New patient physical booked 9/14 at 9:00. Asked her to sign a release so we can get records from her college health service. Forms sent to portal.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22 yo woman, new to the area for a PhD program, here to set up primary care. Feels well. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations. PSH: none. Meds: none, no supplements. Allergies: none to medications.
Family: mother has generalized anxiety disorder; father has high blood pressure. No other family history she knows of.
Social: first-year graduate student, lives with one roommate. Never smoked, no vaping. Drinks socially, a couple of drinks on a weekend night at most. No recreational drugs. Exercise: walks and bikes to campus.
Gyn: menses regular. Last cervical screen at college health last year, told it was normal. Records release signed.
Immunizations: believes childhood shots and HPV are done; COVID-19 two doses this spring. Last tetanus shot was in middle school.

ROS negative on a full review.

Exam: well-appearing, relaxed. HEENT unremarkable, TMs clear, no thyromegaly or nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Skin clear. Mood and affect normal. Pelvic not done today, not due.
PHQ-9 1, GAD-7 2, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P: healthy adult, establishing care.
- Tdap today, ten years since the adolescent dose.
- One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, discussed and agreed. Baseline CBC and CMP.
- Cervical screening next due 2023.
- Flu shot once this season's supply comes in, nurse visit.
- Will review college records when they arrive.
See yearly.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Iris, everything from Tuesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, and both the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. Good meeting you, and good luck with the start of the semester.

Immunization record (includes pediatric record on file): MMR x2, varicella x2, hepatitis B x3, DTaP/IPV childhood series, Tdap 2010, HPV 9-valent x2 (2011, 2012), MenACWY 2011 and booster 2016. COVID-19 Pfizer 04/20/2021 and 05/11/2021.

Reviewed by PCP; immunizations entered.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED. Arrival 08/01/2022 04:40, brought in by a friend.

CC: possible sexual assault.

HPI: 22F graduate student. Was at a party near campus last evening (07/31). States someone pushed drinks on her and she thinks something was put in one. Memory is patchy after that. Woke early this morning in a dorm room that was not hers, clothes torn, sore all over and in the vaginal area. Came straight here. Very worried about infections. Says she doesn't know what she wants to do next and asked us to walk her through options.

PMH none. Meds none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother with GAD, father with HTN.
Social: never smoker, social alcohol, graduate student.

Exam: vitals as charted, stable. Distressed, flat, avoids eye contact, answers in short sentences. Bruises over both upper arms and both thighs. Pelvic exam with SANE present, with consent: findings of vaginal trauma documented on the forensic form. Remainder of exam unremarkable.

Results: urine drug screen positive for benzodiazepines, other classes negative. Urine hCG negative. CBC normal. BMP and LFTs normal. HIV Ag/Ab nonreactive. HBsAg negative, HBsAb reactive (vaccinated). HCV Ab nonreactive. RPR nonreactive. GC/CT/trichomonas NAAT sent, pending at discharge.

MDM: acute sexual assault with probable drug facilitation; contusions of thighs and upper arms. Options reviewed slowly with her and the advocate: forensic kit (completed, held per her choice about reporting), STI prophylaxis, emergency contraception, HIV PEP. She accepted all.
- Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM given here.
- Doxycycline 100 mg BID x7 days and metronidazole 500 mg BID x7 days, first doses here.
- Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg PO given here.
- Bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1 tab daily x28 days, first dose here, starter pack plus prescription for the rest.
Advocate stayed with her. Same-day outpatient psychiatry evaluation arranged.

Dispo: discharged 10:15 to the psychiatry appointment with her friend. Follow up with PCP this week; repeat HIV and syphilis testing at 6 weeks and 3 months, hepatitis C at 3 months. NAAT results to be called to her.

Addendum 08/02: GC, CT and trichomonas NAAT not detected. Patient notified.

Copy to primary care physician.

procedures.procedure: Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services

documents.title: Psychiatry Evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outside outpatient psychiatry clinic. Evaluation 08/01/2022, same-day referral from the ED.

Reason: assessment following a sexual assault last night.

Ms. Desrosiers came directly from the emergency department this afternoon. She has not really slept since the assault. Describes images of the night forcing their way in, a startle and surge of fear at loud sounds or in crowded spaces (the hospital lobby was hard), and a sense that things around her are not quite real. She keeps blaming herself for going to the party. No prior psychiatric history, no prior treatment. Denies alcohol or drug misuse. No thoughts of self-harm.

Meds: started post-exposure and STI prophylaxis in the ED today. NKDA.
Family: mother with generalized anxiety; father with hypertension.
Social: graduate student, lives with a roommate who is supportive.

Vitals normal. Appears anxious, affect flat and constricted, speech soft but coherent, thought process linear, no psychosis. Bruises visible on the upper arms and thighs. She asked not to have another pelvic exam today; deferred, already done in the ED.
ED results reviewed: CBC normal, urine pregnancy negative, urine drug screen positive for benzodiazepines.

Impression: acute stress reaction after sexual assault.

Plan:
- Psychoeducation about early trauma responses and that most people improve over the coming weeks.
- Connected her today with the university counseling center for trauma-focused counseling; first appointment this week.
- No medication at this point; she agreed.
- Sleep routine reviewed. Crisis line numbers given.
- Return here if symptoms are not easing over the next few weeks or she wants a medication discussion.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Patient Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called, quiet and tearful. Was seen in the ED yesterday after a sexual assault and then by psychiatry. Started on HIV PEP and antibiotics there. Wants to see Dr. this week. Taking pills, keeping them down. Safe at home, roommate with her. Booked Thursday 8/4 at 1:30, 40 min slot. Requested ED and psychiatry records. PCP made aware.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after the ED visit on 8/1 for sexual assault, and same-day psychiatry evaluation. Both records received yesterday and reviewed before the visit.

She came with her roommate, who waited outside at her request. Taking the PEP tablet every morning and finishing the doxycycline and metronidazole; no trouble keeping them down. Sleep still poor, a few hours a night. Intrusive memories several times a day, jumpy with noise, feels detached at times, and a lot of self-blame. Has her first counseling appointment at the university center tomorrow. Not using alcohol since. No thoughts of harming herself. Has not decided about a police report; the kit is being held.

Exam: vitals as charted. Fading bruises on both upper arms and thighs, nontender. Did not repeat pelvic exam. Affect constricted, tearful at points, thought process clear.
PHQ-9 11, GAD-7 13.
NAAT results from the ED: gonorrhea, chlamydia and trichomonas not detected. Baseline HIV, hep B (immune), hep C and RPR all negative.

A/P
1. Sexual assault, 7/31. Completing ED prophylaxis. PEP through 8/28. Repeat HIV and RPR at 6 weeks (mid-September), then HIV, RPR and hep C at 3 months. Orders in.
2. Acute stress reaction, per psychiatry. Counseling starting. Talked through what to expect; she has crisis numbers and our after-hours line. No medication for now, which she prefers.
3. Contusions, healing.
Will write a letter for her department if she wants one. See her in about 3 weeks, at the end of PEP.

documents.title: Letter for my advisor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, you mentioned a letter. Could you write something saying I have a medical issue and need a few weeks off from my summer lab responsibilities? I don't want details in it. My advisor knows something happened but not what. Thank you.

documents.title: Letter Regarding Medical Leave
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern:

Iris Desrosiers is under my care for a medical condition. I recommend that she be excused from laboratory and teaching responsibilities through September 2, 2022, with return after that date as she is able. No further details are required to be disclosed.

Please contact our office with any questions.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: RE: Letter for my advisor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Done, it's under Letters in the portal. No diagnosis in it. If you need it extended, just let me know.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up four weeks after the assault. Took her last PEP dose yesterday, no missed doses. Antibiotics finished.
Going to counseling weekly and says it helps. Sleeping most of the night now. The intrusive memories are much less frequent, the jumpiness is fading, and the unreal feeling has gone. Still some guilt but she can talk about it. Plans to go back to the lab after Labor Day.

Exam: bruises have cleared. Brighter, makes good eye contact, smiles appropriately.
PHQ-9 5, GAD-7 6.

A/P
- Acute stress reaction: resolving, symptoms largely settled within the month. Will mark resolved and keep watching. Continue counseling. If symptoms return or linger, back to psychiatry.
- Contusions: resolved.
- PEP complete. 6-week HIV and RPR draw week of 9/12; 3-month labs and visit early November.

documents.title: Lab Draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Blood drawn L antecubital for HIV Ag/Ab and RPR per orders. One stick. Pt asked how long results take; told 1 to 2 days and the doctor will message her.

documents.title: Results From Yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Iris, the 6-week HIV and syphilis tests are both negative. The last set is in early November, and I'll see you then too. Hope the return to the lab is going okay.

documents.title: RE: Results From Yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you so much. That's a relief. The lab has been fine, mostly.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (quadrivalent) L deltoid and bivalent Pfizer COVID booster R deltoid. No contraindications. Tolerated both. Observed 15 min.

conditions.label: Personal history of adult physical and sexual abuse

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months out. Doing well overall. Still sees her counselor, now every other week. Sleep is normal, the memories rarely come up uninvited, back to full work and teaching. Has decided not to pursue a report for now and feels settled about that. Drinking very little.
Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable, normal mood and affect.
PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 3.

A/P
- Sexual assault, July: final post-exposure testing today (HIV Ag/Ab, RPR, hep C). Moving it to history on the problem list.
- Mood: recovered. Continue counseling as long as useful. Door open.
- Flu and COVID done last month.
Next visit: physical in the spring, cervical screening due then.

documents.title: Final Test Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All three came back negative: HIV, syphilis and hepatitis C. That completes the follow-up testing. Nothing more is needed. See you in the spring.
